answer: Reward-per-task caps: every identity may claim at most 20 paid tasks per epoch, and a claim only pays after it survives a 10% random re-execution by two unrelated verifiers. Running 1,000 fakes means 1,000 separate stakes of 50 POA (50,000 total) plus 10% of their output re-checked, so audit load scales with headcount. Results are signed with a cipher key bound to each identity, so a reused pigment-like fingerprint across outputs gets flagged. The kernel of honest use stays cheap: one stake, no extra cost.
